labeller: Labels drafted by an AI assistant (Claude) on behalf of the student, reading the exported chunk text; the student must re-read results/audit_*.csv and confirm or change each label before submission. Risk of bias: labeller also built the pipeline and saw Hit scores before labelling.

coherence.scale: 0 = cut mid-idea / missing subject so not understandable; 1 = partly understandable, missing context; 2 = self-contained, keeps the whole idea
coherence.sampling: Fixed before scoring: middle character of unit 2 of the first 10 documents (sorted) with >=2 units. C uses B's chunks so C = B.

labels.A_reason: starts mid-sentence ('be conducted via...'), ends mid-word ('or t')
starts inside a code example, ends mid-word ('inde')
labels.B_reason: full paragraph but only the first of the 'acceptable options' examples

starts 's are subtype of real numbers', example cut before conclusion
labels.B_reason: both examples complete incl. the List[int] counter-example

metadata.checked: 5 test questions x top-3 = 15 records per strategy: document_id/source, page (chunk text found verbatim in the cited unit), pep_type (vs PEP header), section (heading exists in that unit and is the heading in effect at chunk start).

filter_compliance_all_filter_questions.B_if_filter_were_required: 0/5 questions fully compliant (7/15 records in scope)

issues: A t01 rank1 pep-0008:p011:c002: section='Package and Module Names' is correct by definition (heading at chunk start) but the useful content is under 'Class Names' -> misleading for a human; 117/877 A chunks span >1 section vs 7/532 for B.

page is a synthetic unit index (>=1500 chars), not a printed page: traceable via data/manifest.json char ranges but not citeable like a PDF page.

grounding.scale: 0 = no evidence in top-3; 1 = evidence present but missing a needed condition/context; 2 = enough to answer and trace the source
